title: Approval persistence failure can prevent process cancellation

significance.impact: An owned provider process can remain uncancelled when recording approval closure fails.
significance.exposure: Uncommitted native approval candidate beneath the still-disabled on-request production route. No live grant or provider action was dispatched.
significance.detectability: Ordinary happy-path records do not reveal this lifecycle sequence.
significance.systemic_implication: Approval lifetime must remain separate from projection freshness and fallible persistence.
significance.recovery: Source repair and bounded regressions are possible; no historical provider-side effect was established.
significance.rationale: A material failure of the new approval boundary, contained before production enablement.

confidence.basis: Independent source review and failure-sensitive local reproductions; no native action execution claim.

evidence.observation: The attempt-read, closure-write, and sibling-shutdown regressions all failed at cancellation-signal assertions before the repair.

claim.failure_mode: Cancellation signals were set only after fallible attempt reads and approval closure; shutdown abandoned sibling cancellation and joining on the first error.
claim.downstream_consequence: The user can receive a cancellation error while provider work continues, including siblings during shutdown.

counterevidence.observation: Production on-request routes remain rejected before execution.

proof_limits: This finding was discovered in an uncommitted candidate based on the named Git revision; reviewed candidate hashes are preserved in ledger-review.md.
Local tests do not establish native delivery, execution, same-user credential isolation, or installed-route qualification.

remediation.description: Signal cancellation in finally, continue across shutdown closure failures, join every owned task, then surface all closure errors.

evidence.observation: Signal cancellation in finally, continue across shutdown closure failures, join every owned task, then surface all closure errors.

required: Independently re-examine the repaired lifecycle and test false authority at the intended assertion.
Complete native callback/cancellation and installed-route qualification before E1 closure.
